blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: This paper began with a study of hyperbolic links whose complementary volumes result from evaluations of Feynman diagrams [@9806174]. For each of these volumes we found, by empirical means, a *closed--form* evaluation in terms of a few Clausen functions, evaluated at rational multiples of $\pi$. Then, thanks to generous advice from Don Zagier, we came to appreciate that these results form part of a much larger scaffold, whose unifying feature is the existence of rational relations between hyperbolic volumes and Dedekind zeta values. While the existence of such relations is understood [@DZ:Inve

blocks.title: Dedekind-zeta invariants of closed manifolds
blocks.content: We have found rational Dedekind-zeta invariants for 998 manifolds in the Hodgson--Weeks census, which lists $11,031$ closed orientable manifolds, with 9,218 distinct volumes, all less than $6.5$, and with all their geodesics having lengths greater than $0.3$. These 998 manifolds have 224 distinct volumes, which are rationally related, via ([\[ZK\]](#ZK){reference-type="ref" reference="ZK"},[\[ab\]](#ab){reference-type="ref" reference="ab"}), to 140 distinct Dedekind zeta values, each corresponding to an invariant trace field of at least one census manifold. Table 1 enumerates the fields by deg

blocks.title: Examination of 1,200 single-complex-place fields
blocks.content:
It became clear, from studying [@AMS:JB; @AMS:SB; @AMS:RK; @AMS:DZ], that there are unspecified rational relations of the form ([\[ab\]](#ab){reference-type="ref" reference="ab"}) between Dedekind zeta values and volumes of some, but not all, of the manifolds in the Hodgson--Weeks census. We soon found that 30 of the first 32 census manifolds have rational Dedekind-zeta invariants, with $a\le46$ and $b\le3$. The 2 exceptions are manifolds ${\rm m}003(-4,1)$ and ${\rm m}004(+7,1)$, whose invariant trace fields have 2 complex places.

blocks.title: Examination of 44 fields found by Snap
blocks.content:
For the remaining $140-96=44$ results of Tables 2--12, we made reference to the impressive body of files[^1] at the University of Melbourne. These were obtained by Coulson, Goodman, Hodgson and Neumann [@CGHN] (hereafter referred to as CGHN) using 50-digit precision, in marked distinction to the 5 digits which suffice for the findings above.

CGHN make no reference to Dedekind zeta values; they do, however, find single-complex-place invariant trace fields for about 9% of the Hodgson--Weeks manifolds. The next step was to examine the overlap between our single-complex-place fields and theirs. W

How may one derive/ the rational invariant?
Cusped manifolds and join fields
blocks.content: Now we turn to the study of cusped manifolds, complementary to knots and links. Packaged with SnapPea [@SnapPea], there are the 4,815 orientable cusped manifolds of the Hildebrand--Weeks census [@HiW], triangulated by no more than 7 ideal tetrahedra, and 114 non-orientable manifolds, triangulated by no more than 5. Making $4929\times1200$ comparisons with the Dedekind zeta values of Section 2.1, we found 7 new single-complex-place fields, beyond those from the Hodgson--Weeks census. blocks.title: Links whose volumes link Clausen values
blocks.content:
Our order of presentation is the reverse of the order in which we obtained results. Our primary motivation was to elucidate connections between Clausen values, revealed by studies of Feynman diagrams [@9806174], on which we comment in Section 5.

This section concerns links whose rational Dedekind-zeta invariants link Clausen values. An example is provided by the attractive alternating[^1] link of Fig. 1, discovered as a result of work on light-by-light scattering, reported in Section 5. A second is provided by the non-alternating[^2] daisy-chain link of Fig. 2. These form part of our study of

blocks.title: Signpost: integer sequence A003657
blocks.content: Mathematically speaking, the results of Section 2, while numerically striking, are of a rational character [@DZ:Invent; @DZ:JMPS; @DZ:Texel] that was expected by specialists of $K$-theory (which we are not). The challenge is not to understand why a rational Dedekind-zeta invariant exists, but to learn how to derive (as opposed to measure) it. The cusped results of Section 3 were of the same character as for closed manifolds: hyperbolic knots and links have rational Dedekind-zeta invariants if their complementary cusped manifolds have single-complex-place invariant trace fields. blocks.title: Dirichlet character
blocks.content:
The simplest example of a number field with a single complex place is an imaginary-quadratic field ${\bf Q}(\sqrt{-d})$, where $d$ is a square-free positive integer. When $d\equiv3$ (mod 4), the discriminant is $D=-d$; otherwise it is $D=-4d$.

It is proven in [@Berndt] that $$\frac{\zeta_K(2)}{\zeta(2)}=\sum_{n>0}\frac{\chi_K(n)}{n^2}\label{chi}$$ where $\chi_K$ is the real Dirichlet character of the group of units of the field ${\bf Z}/|D|$ and $D$ is the discriminant of the imaginary-quadratic field $K$. blocks.title: Figure-8 knot at $D=-3$
blocks.content:
The first case, at $D=-3$, is elementary. The unique[^1] arithmetic knot is the figure-8 knot of Fig. 3. Its volume is the first entry of Table 19. It links Clausen values at $2\arctan\sqrt3$ and $2\pi/3$. This relation clearly poses no analytical puzzle, since the angles are identical.

[^1]: See Helaman Ferguson's sculpture at ` http://www.mtholyoke.edu/acad/math/ma/sculpture.htm`

blocks.title: Whitehead link at $D=-4$
blocks.content: Just as the simplest hyperbolic knot, $4_1$, gave the answer at $D=-3$, so the simplest hyperbolic 2-component link, namely the Whitehead link $5^2_1$ of Fig. 4, gives the answer at $D=-4$. Its volume is the second entry of Table 19. It links Clausen values at $2\arctan\sqrt1$ and $2\pi/4$, which are again identical.

blocks.title: A self-dual platonic link at $D=-20$
blocks.content:
The reader might now expect us to consider the case $D=-19$. For reasons that will be given in Section 5, we skip to $D=-20$, where we were rewarded by the splendidly symmetric alternating platonic link drawn in Fig. 1. Its Dedekind-zeta invariant was measured to be unity. This innocent-sounding statement translates to our 5th unproven relation $$36{\rm Cl}_2(\theta_5)-30{\rm Cl}_2(2\theta_5)

blocks.title: A 48-crossing daisy-chain link at $D=-24$
blocks.content:
The attentive reader will now expect us to skip the case $D=-23$ and jump to the 8th underlining in ([\[iq\]](#iq){reference-type="ref" reference="iq"}), at $D=-24$. This is precisely what we did, though the character of the result was not what we first supposed. It seemed to us that the hallmark of past success, in finding links that link Clausen values, was to achieve the largest possible symmetry group. What, we asked ourselves, could pack a better symmetry-to-crossing ratio than the remaining 4 platonic alternating links?

blocks.title: Quartic platonic links
blocks.content:
Our first guess, that the 4 non-self-dual platonic links might yield quadratic number fields, failed. Nonetheless, it is interesting to determine their number fields, and hence obtain accurate volumes. This is clearly a taxing job. To prepare for it, we first tackled a problem of similar complexity, where an accurate answer could be inferred.

We found that by adding $n$ concentric components at each of the 4 "vertices" of Fig. 1, one obtains a volume $Z_{20}+2nZ_{15}$ for the link with $24+24n$ crossings and $10+4n$ components, when $n\le5$. At $n=6$, SnapPea was given the 34-component link w

blocks.title: Knots and links from Feynman diagrams
blocks.content: Finally, we arrive at the motivating idea for this work: values of Feynman diagrams.

Following work that involved comparable Clausen values [@Sixth; @Ising], it was observed in [@9806174] that light-by-light scattering yields remarkable results at $s=t=n\in\{4,5,6,7\}$, where the dilogs give rational multiples of the volumes of links.

blocks.title: Hyperbolic Feynman links
blocks.content:
In [@DD], Andrei Davydychev and Bob Delbourgo made a fine discovery: the dilogarithms of the box diagram for particle scattering are those which give the volume of a tetrahedron in hyperbolic 3-space (or its analytic continuation).

In the 3-dimensional [@Nickel] studies of statistical physics, one-loop Feynman diagrams yield logarithms; in the 4 space-time dimensions of relativistic quantum field theory (QFT), they yield dilogarithms [@tHV]. A connection between the dilogs of QFT and those of hyperbolic geometry was considered in [@OW]. The achievement of [@DD] is to derive a fairly simple re

blocks.content:
The rationale for the underlinings in ([\[iq\]](#iq){reference-type="ref" reference="iq"}) should now be clear: it was these 10 imaginary-quadratic fields that had been distinguished by the Feynman orthoschemes of Table 22, which initiated our studies. For 4 of these 10 fields, the census gave links; for 2 of the remaining 6, the work in [@9806174] gave links; for 2 of the remaining 4, the alternating platonic link of Fig. 1 and the non-alternating daisy-chain link of Fig. 2 supplied answers; that left us with the $D=-39$ and $D=-84$ links still missing.

blocks.title: Dedekind zeta values from 12-crossing Feynman knots
blocks.content:
At 12 crossings, corresponding to 8 loops in QFT, Broadhurst and Kreimer [@BK15] found that 7 of the 2,176 hyperbolic knots are positive. We found that 3 of these have rational Dedekind-zeta invariants, with $$\begin{aligned}

\label{1515}\\

2\times{\rm vol}(\sigma_1^{3}\sigma_2^{3}\sigma_1^{3}\sigma_2^{3})
\label{3333}
\end{aligned}$$ The first two are those identified as Feynman knots in [@BGK; @BK15]. Again

blocks.title: Dedekind zeta values from maximally symmetric knots
blocks.content:
Jim Hoste, Morwen Thistlethwaite and Jeff Weeks (hereafter HTW) have recently completed an impressive symmetry analysis [@HTW] of all 1,701,936 prime knots with up to 16 crossings. From the University of Tennessee at Knoxville, we obtained files[^1] that identify highly symmetric alternating and non-alternating knots at crossing numbers from 11 to 16. Before analyzing the most symmetric of these, we comment on the situation up to 10 crossings, in territory charted by Dale Rolfsen [@Rolfsen] and predecessors.
